mt: 'COAUTHOR DATASET' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE DATASET AT A FINER GRAIN THAN THE CENSUS'S SOURCE, FROM ITS OWN SITE; THE WRITERS GIVEN AS CROWD WORKERS AND THE TEXT DIVIDED BY PERCENTAGE
d: THE DATASET, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The CoAuthor Dataset is a large-scale, process-oriented dataset capturing human-AI collaborative writing interactions developed by researchers Mina Lee, Percy Liang, and Qian Yang (CHI 2022).' Statistics (1,445 sessions; '63 qualified crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk'; 830 stories by 58 writers, 615 essays by 49; 'Suggestion acceptance rate: 72.3%'; 'Human-authored text proportion: 72.6%'); keystroke-level logging; the Tab-key interface; davinci configurations; access (the Stanford site, GitHub, ACM, arXiv:2201.06796). Five cards: Stanford University, arXiv, ACM Digital Library, GitHub, alphaXiv.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the dataset, the Overview gives its authors, size, composition, mechanics and where to get it, from its site, its paper and its code.
findings: THE DATASET AT A FINER GRAIN. The arXiv abstract, the census row's one source: 'CoAuthor captures rich interactions between 63 writers and four instances of GPT-3 across 1445 writing sessions.' The composition adds the split by genre, the prompt sources (r/WritingPrompts, The New York Times), the averages and rates, from the Stanford card ('Creative writing: 830 stories written by 58 writers Argumentative writing: 615 essays written by 49 writers'). The census row: 'the dataset's home page could not be read' and 'whether the site and replay interface answer today is unrecorded'. The site is indexed and carded on 2026-11-01, and the code repository with it ('GitHub - minalee-research/coauthor-interface').

THE WRITERS AS CROWD WORKERS. 'Participants: 63 qualified crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk'. The census row: 'the abstract counts 63 writers and does not say whether or how they are named'. The composition says where the writers were recruited and names none of them.

THE TEXT DIVIDED BY PERCENTAGE. 'Human-authored text proportion: 72.6%.' The census row's function field: 'how authorship of a session's text is assigned is not recorded in the saved source'. The composition gives an aggregate share of human-authored text, a measure the saved abstract does not carry; the measure is of the dataset, and no session's text is assigned to anyone.

THE COLLABORATOR NOT CARRIED. The abstract reads the model's part as 'its contribution as a writing "collaborator" under various definitions of good collaboration'. The composition gives the interaction as rates ('Queries per session: 11.8 queries') and its follow-up offers 'specific findings regarding human-AI collaboration' without stating any.
analysis: The dataset composed more finely than the census's saved abstract allows, from the dataset's own site, which the census could not read. It counts the writers, recruits them from a crowd platform and divides the text by percentage; the abstract's frame, the model as 'collaborator' under definitions of collaboration, is not carried.
per_note: The three authors named; Stanford and ACM named; arXiv:2201.06796 given; site, paper and code carded.
